profiles.name: GPT Image 2 — Text to Image
rules: For production shots, references carry identity; the prompt carries geometry, action, lighting, and grade.
Describe physical contact points and frame-relative sides explicitly.
Specify every plot-bearing word exactly, including position, font character, color, and size; otherwise leave text blank.
Keep sharp foreground detail while placing haze and atmosphere in the midground/background.
Do not use film titles as style references in the model prompt.

profiles.name: GPT Image 2 — Blocking Frame
rules: Create flat greyscale storyboard blocking with simple masses, clear silhouettes, and readable depth separation.
Use labelled placeholders rather than production identity, wardrobe, materials, colour, texture, lighting, or era detail.
Preserve the project aspect ratio so staged positions remain useful for the production frame.
Render only the requested element labels and no other text.

blockingSettings.outputSize: Match the project aspect ratio; use a modest long edge suitable for disposable planning
blockingSettings.note: Fast default for inexpensive storyboard blocking.

profiles.name: GPT Image 2 — Reference Edit
rules: Begin with: Keep everything identical and change ONLY the named detail.
Always state: Do NOT mirror the image.
Pin unchanged text verbatim and forbid subject/object relocation.
Use one surgical edit; if the frame becomes tired, fidelity-upscale or restart from the clean source.
Do not edit a hand or paw into a new pose when a clean destination frame can be generated instead.

profiles.name: GPT Image 2 — Multi-reference Composite
rules: Assign every image one job.
Specify which reference controls identity, wardrobe, location, prop, composition, lighting or style.
State what must not be imported from each reference.

profiles.name: Nano Banana 2 — Text to Image
rules: Use complete natural-language production direction.
Be explicit about spatial relationships.
State the intended production asset and aspect ratio.
Keep canon constraints separate from creative direction.

profiles.name: Nano Banana 2 — Blocking Frame
rules: Create flat greyscale storyboard blocking with simple masses, clear silhouettes, and readable depth separation.
Use labelled placeholders rather than production identity, wardrobe, materials, colour, texture, lighting, or era detail.
Preserve the project aspect ratio so staged positions remain useful for the production frame.
Render only the requested element labels and no other text.

blockingSettings.outputSize: Match the project aspect ratio; use a modest long edge suitable for disposable planning
blockingSettings.note: Fast alternate blocking profile for simple layouts.

profiles.name: Nano Banana 2 — Edit
rules: Name the base image.
Describe the exact visual delta.
Explicitly preserve all unrelated pixels, design details and framing.
Avoid restaging unless requested.

profiles.name: Nano Banana 2 — Multi-reference
rules: Give each reference a concrete role.
Explain how to combine them without copying unwanted pose, background or style.
Prefer direct spatial language over tag lists.

profiles.name: Nano Banana Pro — Text to Image
rules: Use for difficult spatial compositions, typography and high-stakes frames.
Define foreground, midground and background.
State character-to-character and character-to-prop relationships precisely.

profiles.name: Nano Banana Pro — Blocking Frame
rules: Create flat greyscale storyboard blocking with simple masses, clear silhouettes, and readable depth separation.
Define foreground, midground, background, and character-to-prop relationships precisely for difficult spatial compositions.
Use labelled placeholders rather than production identity, wardrobe, materials, colour, texture, lighting, or era detail.
Preserve the project aspect ratio so staged positions remain useful for the production frame.
Render only the requested element labels and no other text.

blockingSettings.outputSize: Match the project aspect ratio; use a modest long edge suitable for disposable planning
blockingSettings.note: Use when the shot has difficult spatial relationships or layered foreground/midground/background blocking.

profiles.name: Nano Banana Pro — Edit
rules: State the base image and exact target state.
Break complex edits into ordered changes.
Protect composition, identity and lighting in a preserve list.

profiles.name: Nano Banana Pro — Multi-reference
rules: Assign every reference a role and prohibited contribution.
Use explicit layout and overlap instructions.
State which source wins if references conflict.

profiles.name: FLUX.2 — Text to Image
rules: Lead with strong visual nouns and spatial relationships.
Specify materials, lens, lighting and palette.
Keep exclusions concise and concrete.
Do not use booru tag soup.

profiles.name: FLUX.2 — Reference Edit
rules: Identify the base image.
Describe changed objects, positions and materials precisely.
Protect all unmentioned content.
Use color and material terms when continuity matters.

profiles.name: FLUX.2 — Multi-reference Composite
rules: Assign references by visual role.
State exact screen positions and scale.
Define which image contributes identity, material, prop, lighting and style.

profiles.name: Seedream 5 Pro — Text to Image
rules: Use natural-language art direction.
Define layout, subject hierarchy and production purpose.
Make reference assignments explicit.
Treat provider limits as editable until verified.

profiles.name: Seedream 5 Pro — Edit
rules: State the source image and exact change.
Protect unedited identity, geometry, lighting and color.
Use ordered instructions for complex edits.

profiles.name: Seedream 5 Pro — Multi-reference
rules: Define each reference role and conflict priority.
State precise spatial relationships and intended final composition.
Protect canon identity and design anchors.

profiles.name: Krea 2 — Visual Exploration
rules: Separate content from art direction.
Use for look development, moodboards and style discovery rather than final continuity edits.
State what style references may influence and what they must not copy.

profiles.name: Krea 2 — Reference Edit
rules: Name the approved base plate and the exact visual change.
Use additional images only for their assigned identity, prop, or design role.
Preserve the base composition, camera, lighting logic, geometry, and all unrelated details.
Do not mirror or restage unless explicitly requested.

profiles.name: Krea 2 — Multi-reference Composite
rules: Assign every reference one explicit content, identity, prop, location, composition, or style job.
State screen position, scale, pose, contact points, and reference conflict priority.
Protect approved identity and design anchors while excluding unwanted source backgrounds or poses.

profiles.name: Krea 2 — Style Reference
rules: Assign content and style references separately.
State style weights as guidance.
Do not copy subjects or objects from style-only references.

profiles.name: Krea 2 — Moodboard
rules: Summarize the shared visual language across references.
Name palette, materials, lighting, texture and framing rhythm.
Avoid importing recognizable subjects from references.

profiles.name: Seedance 2 — Text to Video
rules: Describe one continuous shot chronologically.
Separate subject performance, camera movement and environment motion.
Fit the number of actions to duration.
State exact dialogue and audio only when requested.

profiles.name: Seedance 2 — Image to Video
rules: Use only the approved start frame unless the task is explicitly reference-led.
Describe one positively named subject action plus useful ambient life.
Scope stillness to the body; do not flood the prompt with motionless/still negatives.
Avoid the word flicker for practical lights; use steady even glow and put motion into smoke, rain, dust, or screen content.
Keep the prompt to one to three short sentences and use mid-range dynamics for subtle-life shots.
For long near-still shots, generate a shorter living section and extend or hold the tail in post.

profiles.name: Seedance 2 — First / Last Frame
rules: Both endpoint compositions must exist as approved real frames.
Describe only the physical transition; do not ask FLF to invent a new framing or materialize an object.
Flag scale/framing mismatches and recommend i2v → insert → held-end or chained clips.
Do camera movement and lip-sync as separate passes.
End exactly on the supplied final frame and hold briefly when the endpoint will be reused for a match cut.

profiles.name: Seedance 2 — Omni Reference
rules: Assign every image, video and audio input one explicit job.
Use image references for identity, wardrobe, composition, props or opening state; use video references only for motion, performance, effects or camera behavior.
Use audio references for timing, dialogue delivery, music rhythm or sound design and state the intended relationship explicitly.
References carry source information; the prompt states the desired shot geometry, action, camera, timing and invariants.
Do not ask one reference to control several conflicting attributes.
Keep one continuous shot within the selected duration.

profiles.name: MiniMax H3 — Text to Video
rules: Write the visual direction in chronological order.
Use timed blocks whenever the shot contains more than one beat.
Direct sound, dialogue, ambience and music as deliberately as the picture.
Keep the action physically plausible inside 5–15 seconds.
Avoid vague camera language and conflicting simultaneous actions.

Keep this written package within CineBraid's own 2,000-character brevity budget; preserve reference assignments, chronology, continuity locks, and audio before optional stylistic detail. The dispatch ceiling is a separate question, resolved from model and backend capability at generation time.

profiles.name: MiniMax H3 — Image to Video
rules: Image 1 is the exact opening frame and already defines identity, composition, lighting and style.
Describe the motion that begins from Image 1 instead of re-describing the whole image.
Separate subject performance, camera movement, environment motion and sound.
Use timed blocks only when the clip contains more than one beat.

Keep this written package within CineBraid's own 2,000-character brevity budget; preserve reference assignments, chronology, continuity locks, and audio before optional stylistic detail. The dispatch ceiling is a separate question, resolved from model and backend capability at generation time.

profiles.name: MiniMax H3 — First / Last Frame
rules: Image 1 is the exact opening frame and Image 2 is the exact final frame.
Describe only the plausible bridge between the two endpoints.
Keep identity, wardrobe, location geometry and screen direction stable.
Use chronological timing when the bridge has multiple beats.
Do not invent cuts, new props or extra story beats unless explicitly requested.

Keep this written package within CineBraid's own 2,000-character brevity budget; preserve reference assignments, chronology, continuity locks, and audio before optional stylistic detail. The dispatch ceiling is a separate question, resolved from model and backend capability at generation time.

profiles.name: MiniMax H3 — Multi-Frame / Reference Video
rules: Assign an explicit job to every Image, Video and Audio reference.
When approved shot frames are supplied in order, state that Images 1–N are sequential keyframes and describe the transition between each pair.
Use timed shot-list blocks for more than one beat.
Do not let sequential keyframes become a slideshow; describe continuous motion, transitions, camera behavior and settling at each beat.
Use reference video only for the assigned motion, performance, camera rhythm or source-video edit.
Direct native stereo audio deliberately and identify any Audio reference by number.
Keep the total reference package within 12 files: at most 9 images, 3 videos and 3 audio clips.

Keep this written package within CineBraid's own 2,000-character brevity budget; preserve reference assignments, chronology, continuity locks, and audio before optional stylistic detail. The dispatch ceiling is a separate question, resolved from model and backend capability at generation time.

profiles.name: Kling 3 — Text to Video
rules: Lead with subject and motion.
Add background motion and one clear camera move.
Avoid stacking many independent actions.
Keep physical language direct.
Quote exact dialogue and keep sound direction synchronized when native audio is requested.

profiles.name: Kling 3 — Image to Video
rules: Use exactly one starting image.
The image already defines subject, location, composition, lighting and style.
Describe only subject movement, important background movement and an intentional camera move.
Use one short natural-language paragraph; omit reference maps, preserve blocks and negative lists.
Quote exact dialogue and keep sound direction synchronized when native audio is requested.

profiles.name: Kling 3 — First / Last Frame
rules: Use exactly the supplied first and last frames.
Describe the simplest physical transition between them.
Mention camera movement only when needed to connect the frames.
Do not repeat visual details already established by the frames or add preserve/avoid blocks.
Quote exact dialogue and keep sound direction synchronized when native audio is requested.

profiles.name: Kling 3 — Motion / Reference Control
rules: Distinguish identity, source frame and motion reference.
State that motion references control timing only unless otherwise specified.
Keep camera and subject motion separate.
Quote exact dialogue and keep sound direction synchronized when native audio is requested.

profiles.name: LTX 2.3 — Text to Video
rules: Write a detailed literal chronological paragraph.
Include gestures, environment, camera, lighting and notable changes.
Keep under roughly 200 words.
Include synchronized audio only when enabled.

profiles.name: LTX 2.3 — Image to Video
rules: Treat the first frame as exact visual ground truth.
Write a chronological flowing paragraph.
Include performance, camera, lighting changes, foley and ambience where useful.
Preserve identity and geometry.

profiles.name: LTX 2.3 — First / Last Frame
rules: Describe the literal chronological bridge between frames.
Make body, object, camera and lighting transitions physically plausible.
Finish exactly at the supplied final frame.

profiles.name: LTX 2.3 — Synchronized Audio / Video
rules: Integrate dialogue, foley and ambience at the moment they occur.
Quote exact dialogue and assign the speaker.
Keep visual and audio chronology synchronized.

profiles.name: Happy Horse 1.1 — Image to Video
rules: Use one starting image for image-to-video.
Describe only visible movement and intentional camera movement.
Add dialogue, sound effects or ambience only when they are deliberately requested.
Use a short natural-language paragraph; omit reference maps, appearance summaries, preserve blocks and negative lists.

profiles.name: Happy Horse 1.1 — Dialogue / Reference Performance
rules: Map every character reference.
Assign each spoken line and non-speaking reaction.
State performance timing, tone and body movement.
Define ambience, foley and unwanted sound.

profiles.name: Wan 2.7 — Text to Video
rules: Describe subject, action, environment and camera in chronological order.
Avoid conflicting movement directions.
Keep one dominant action per short clip.

profiles.name: Wan 2.7 — Image to Video
rules: Use the approved start frame as visual ground truth and describe only motion/camera.
For text-critical or high-stillness work, use 1080p and LOW motion strength.
Use Wan’s real negative field for camera movement, warping, text morphing, hands entering, and motion blur.
Do not use Enhance after suppressing motion.

profiles.name: Wan 2.7 — First / Last Frame
rules: Use exactly two approved layout-compatible endpoint frames.
Keep text and geometry identical where they must interpolate without swimming.
Use 1080p and low motion strength for text-bearing inserts.
Put unwanted camera and morphing behavior in the negative field; do not Enhance.

profiles.name: Wan 2.7 — Reference to Video
rules: Assign identity, location, prop, pose and motion references.
State reference priority when they conflict.
Keep camera and performance instructions separate.

profiles.name: Wan 2.7 — Video Edit
rules: Identify the source video and requested change.
List what timing, performance, camera and environment must remain unchanged.
Avoid restaging unrelated content.

profiles.name: LTX 2.3 — Video Retake
rules: Describe only the requested change inside the selected time range.
Preserve everything outside the retake section.
State whether video, audio, or both should be replaced.
Keep continuity with the frames immediately before and after the edited section.
